cases.title: Intake and Handoffs, Automated
cases.p1_html: Problem. Creative requests arrived by too many routes, and final assets (design links, copy docs, images) got lost as work moved between related tasks. Native syncing across task levels wasn't available in our setup.
cases.p2_html: What I did. I co-designed and co-built our Asana implementation for marketing requests from scratch, with the team that runs intake, and I handled the technical build. Before writing any automation code, I had Claude Code interview me and test whether the platform could support the idea. Then I built Asana Tasks Family Sync: a rule that carries final assets between related tasks, is safe to re-run, copies cleanly to other projects, and is documented. I paired it with team training so it stuck. Result. Final assets, including design links, copy docs, and video, now follow the work automatically, so nobody has to hunt for the latest file.

cases.title: Analyst Report Programs, Ready Before the Report Lands
cases.p1_html: Problem. An analyst firm published its report earlier than expected.
cases.p2_html: What I did. I'd prepared a contingency plan in advance, with AI help, so we weren't starting from zero. Result. An executive landing page went live within 3 days, against a 14-day plan. I also coordinated marketing for the BigCommerce Payments launch.

meta: Tools: Asana, Asana Node.js SDK, Claude Code
cases.title: Campaign Builder
cases.p1_html: Problem. Setting up a campaign meant rebuilding the same task structure by hand, and the brief and the tasks drifted apart.
cases.p2_html: What I did. I built and piloted a brief-to-project automation in Asana that turns a campaign brief into tasks and dependencies. A pilot run generated a full parent task and its subtasks straight from a brief. I paused the broader rollout until the underlying request data was ready. Result. A working pattern for turning one brief into a complete, routed project, ready to extend.

cases.title: AI Tooling at Work
cases.p1_html: Problem. A marketing work system lives in a lot of people's heads, and incomplete requests turn into rework.
cases.p2_html:
What I'm building. Four AI initiatives, all on tools we already own.
Brief to Campaign: one campaign brief becomes a complete, routed Asana project (built and piloted).
Claude Asana Project: a living operating manual for marketing's work system, in a Claude knowledge base that updates when the rules change (in progress).
AI Intake Triage: catching incomplete requests at the door, before they become rework (in progress).
Automated Status Updates: stakeholders get status without asking, starting with blocked-work alerts (early stage).

about_page.lead: I've always lived in two worlds at once. I'm the nerd who ran IT for a retreat center in Vermont, tested software, and answered support tickets, and I still can't leave a repetitive task alone. I'm also a maker: I write and play music, I've produced video for years, and I love a good pipeline. The two have run side by side the whole way. When they line up, I build things like an Asana setup that keeps creative work from getting lost, or a pipeline that cuts footage while I'm at the park with my family. When they don't, I'm the one in the room who speaks both languages.
